items.title: A proposed order authorizing the Corporation Counsel to enter into and execute a Settlement Order in the following sixteen (16) cases

enrichment.relevance_reason: This item authorizes settlement of sixteen lawsuits against city personnel with a payout of $260,814,000, which does not involve building, financing, regulating, or taxing homes or tenants' rights.

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of an intergovernmental agreement with the Chicago Board of Education to provide TIF funds for improvements at Harriet Beecher Stowe Elementary School, located at 3444 W. Wabansia Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item provides TIF funds for improvements at an elementary school, which is a public institutional use with no housing built, financed, preserved, regulated, or demolished.

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of an intergovernmental agreement with the Chicago Board of Education to provide TIF funds for improvements at Suder Montessori Magnet Elementary School, located at 2022 W. Washington Boulevard.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item provides TIF funds for capital improvements at a public elementary school, which is an educational facility and not about homes, housing finance, or residential rights.

items.title: A substitute ordinance approving the execution of the 66th amending agreement with SomerCor 504, Inc. to increase the amount of grant funds available in various redevelopment project areas, amend the Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF) program rules, and authorize SomerCor 504, Inc. to continue providing administrative services for the program.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The SBIF program provides grants to small businesses for storefront and commercial property improvements in redevelopment areas, not to homes or residents' housing rights, so it does not bear on housing.

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of a Redevelopment Agreement with BTH Development, NFP to provide Housing and Economic Development Bond (HED) funds for redevelopment of Altgeld Gardens Youth Center project at 13122 S. Ellis Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item funds a youth center redevelopment at Altgeld Gardens, a community facility, and the material describes no housing units or housing activity.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing a Redevelopment Agreement with BTH Development, NFP for up to $7,300,000 in Housing and Economic Development Bond (HED) funds to redevelop the Altgeld Gardens Youth Center at 13122 S. Ellis Avenue (10th Ward).

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of a Redevelopment Agreement with North Lawndale Catalyst Initiative, NFP to provide Housing and Economic Development (HED) funds and tax increment financing (TIF) assistance for the Filmore Linen Services project at 920-922 S. Campbell Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item funds a Filmore Linen Services project, which appears to be a commercial or economic development project, and the material mentions no housing.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing a Redevelopment Agreement with North Lawndale Catalyst Initiative, NFP for up to $5,000,000 in HED funds and up to $5,000,000 in TIF assistance for the Filmore Linen Services project at 920-922 S. Campbell Avenue (28th Ward).

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of a Redevelopment Agreement with Hudson Michigan Avenue Owner LLC to provide Housing and Economic Development (HED) funds for the Hudson House project at 2222 S. Michigan Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance would provide City HED loan and grant funds to a project called Hudson House, which appears to be a housing development financed by the City.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing a Redevelopment Agreement with Hudson Michigan Avenue Owner LLC for Housing and Economic Development (HED) funds for the Hudson House project at 2222 S. Michigan Avenue: up to $5,000,000 as a City loan and up to $10,000,000 as a City grant.

items.title: One (1) proposed order authorizing the payment of various small claims against the City of Chicago.

enrichment.relevance_reason: This item authorizes payments to settle lawsuits against the City, such as the Guevara-related cases, and does not build, finance, regulate, tax, or demolish homes or affect tenants' rights.

items.title: One (1) proposed orders denying the payment of various small claims against the City of Chicago.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item denies payment of various small claims against the City and does not concern homes, housing finance, tax, regulation, or residents' rights in housing.

items.title: Appointment of Vernell Givens as Commissioner of Chicago Housing Authority for a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item is an appointment of a Chicago Housing Authority commissioner, which bears on the governance of public housing.
enrichment.summary: The Committee on Housing and Real Estate will consider the appointment of Vernell Givens as a Chicago Housing Authority Commissioner, for a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

items.title: Appointment of Mary Gardner as Commissioner of Chicago Housing Authority for a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns an appointment to the Chicago Housing Authority board, the body that governs the city's public housing.
enrichment.summary: The Committee on Housing and Real Estate would consider the appointment of Mary Gardner as a Commissioner of the Chicago Housing Authority, with a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

items.title: Appointment of Hipolito (Paul) Roldan as Commissioner of Chicago Housing Authority

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item is a mayoral appointment to the Chicago Housing Authority's board of commissioners, which governs public housing in Chicago.
enrichment.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson has appointed Hipolito (Paul) Roldan as a Chicago Housing Authority commissioner, for a term effective immediately and expiring July 7, 2031. The appointment goes to City Council for consideration.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 11414 S Halsted St to Far South CDC under Low-Income Housing Tax Credits program for redevelopment of Morgan Park Commons (repeal and replacement of O2026-0026567 in entirety)

attachments.label: O2026-0029008 Ex C Site Plan and Project Phases
O2026-0029008 Ex B Legal Description of Dev Property

enrichment.relevance_reason: It authorizes sale of city-owned land to a nonprofit developer for a mixed-income housing redevelopment with affordable units financed under the LIHTC program.
enrichment.summary: Replaces a July 2026 ordinance to authorize selling the City-owned 11414 S Halsted St parcel to Far South CDC for $1 per tax parcel. Morgan Park Commons Phase 1 would add 70 mixed-income units, 66 affordable, with Phase 0 site work funded by a $15 million State grant.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 1335 S Springfield Ave to MKB Business Strategies LLC in Trust for Use of Schools

attachments.label: O2026-0029007 Ex B Depiction of Property

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells a former school site to a developer planning to demolish the building and build 13 single-family houses and 13 affordable three-flats.
enrichment.summary: The City Council would accept MKB Business Strategies, LLC's $25,000 bid for the Board of Education property at 1335 S Springfield Ave. MKB plans to demolish the existing building and build 13 single-family houses and 13 affordable three-flats in two phases.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 2830 W Wilcox St, 2860 W Cermak Rd, 5016 S Christiana Ave, 7713 S Dobson St, 5008, 5010, 5012, 5014, 5016 and 5018 S Throop St to various buyers under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item sells vacant City-owned lots to buyers for community open space under a deed restriction requiring open space improvements, with no homes built, preserved, or regulated, and no change to residential use.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 1948 W 63rd St to Reynoso Insulation LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The sale of two vacant City-owned lots is for a commercial parking lot serving the buyer's adjacent business, with no housing units involved.
enrichment.summary: The City would sell two vacant City-owned lots at 1948 W. 63rd St. to Reynoso Insulation, LLC for $18,006 through ChiBlockBuilder. The buyer plans a new commercial parking lot for its adjacent business.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 2054 and 2058 W Warren Blvd to EGP Warren Apartments LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells city-owned vacant land for a 20-unit residential building that includes four ARO-compliant affordable units.
enrichment.summary: The City Council would approve the sale of city-owned lots at 2054 and 2058 W. Warren Blvd. to EGP Warren Apartments LLC through ChiBlockBuilder for $315,315. The buyer would build a 20-unit residential building with four Affordable Requirements Ordinance units.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 4927, 4935 and 4937 S Forrestville Ave to TK Palos LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells city-owned vacant land for construction of 16 residential units, including ARO units, in Grand Boulevard.
enrichment.summary: The City Council would approve the sale of three city-owned parcels on S Forrestville Ave to TK Palos LLC for $301,028 through ChiBlockBuilder. The buyer would build two 8-unit masonry residential buildings with garages and parking, with ARO units included.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 4549 S Indiana Ave to Click Development LLC 4549 Indiana under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells a city-owned vacant lot for construction of a new 16-unit residential building that includes two ARO units.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance approving the sale of city-owned property at 4549 S. Indiana Ave. to Click Development, LLC 4549 Indiana through ChiBlockBuilder for $203,241. The buyer would build a 16-unit residential building with two ARO units and a six-space parking pad.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 3729, 3731 and 3733 S Giles Ave to Iron Eagle LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item is a sale of three City-owned lots for construction of nine new residential dwelling units under the ChiBlockBuilder program.
enrichment.summary: The City would sell three vacant lots at 3729, 3731 and 3733 S Giles Ave to Iron Eagle LLC for $250,000 under ChiBlockBuilder. Iron Eagle plans three three-story buildings with three 3-bedroom units each, nine homes total, with no ARO units.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 1509 E 67th Pl to 1509 E. 67th PL LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item approves the sale of vacant City-owned land for market-rate residential development through the ChiBlockBuilder program.
enrichment.summary: The City Council would approve selling vacant City-owned property at 1509 E 67th Pl to 1509 E. 67th PL LLC through ChiBlockBuilder for market-rate development, subject to a deed restriction and Department of Planning and Development approval of plans, budget and permits.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 4849, 4853 and 4857 W West End Ave to Medlock Development LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: It approves the sale of city-owned vacant lots for a 15-unit new construction residential project through the ChiBlockBuilder program.
enrichment.summary: City Council would approve the sale of city-owned property at 4849, 4853 and 4857 W West End Ave to Medlock Development LLC through ChiBlockBuilder for market-rate development. The buyer's disclosure describes a 15-unit new construction project.

items.title: President’s Update

enrichment.relevance_reason: The CLIHTF board oversees the Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund, which subsidizes rental housing for low-income tenants, and this is the president's update at its October 2026 meeting.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board of Directors will hear a President's Update at its October 13, 2026 meeting. The agenda item itself has no further detail.

items.title: Reports

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board hears committee reports on rental subsidy allocations, a property ownership change, and the draft 2027 budget.
enrichment.summary: CLIHTF Board of Directors will hear committee reports, including an allocations summary, an ownership change at 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties, financial statements, and the draft 2027 budget.

items.title: Allocations Summary

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board is receiving an allocations summary for its rental subsidy program for low-income tenants.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board of Directors will hear an Allocations Summary from its Allocations Committee, chaired by Adonya Little. The same committee report also covers an ownership change at 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties.

items.title: Ownership change of 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties

enrichment.relevance_reason: A Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund property ownership change affects a rental subsidy property and the tenants who live there.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Allocations Committee will report on an ownership change of 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties.

items.title: Financial Statements as of September 30, 2026

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board reviews its finances, which fund rental subsidies for low-income tenants.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board of Directors will review the Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund's financial statements as of September 30, 2026, as a Finance and Audit Committee report presented by Treasurer Meredith Muir.

items.title: Presentation of draft 2027 Budget

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund's draft 2027 budget bears on funding for its rental subsidy program for low-income tenants.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board of Directors' Finance and Audit Committee will present the draft 2027 budget at the October 13 board meeting.

items.title: Outreach Committee Update provided by Board VP Sam Paler-Ponce

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board hears an outreach committee update, which relates to a rental subsidy program for low-income tenants.
enrichment.summary: Board Vice President Sam Paler-Ponce will give the Outreach Committee update at the CLIHTF Board of Directors meeting on October 13, 2026.

items.title: New Business: Tenant Outreach Initiative presented by Marlana Edwards, Director of Program Development and Outreach

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board will hear a tenant outreach initiative tied to its rental subsidy program for low-income renters.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board of Directors will hear a Tenant Outreach Initiative presentation from Marlana Edwards, Director of Program Development and Outreach, under new business at its October 13 meeting.

items.title: Establishment of Problem Landlord and Housing Court Coordination Task Force to examine and recommend improvements to response to chronic and repeat housing code violations

enrichment.relevance_reason: The resolution creates a task force on problem landlords and repeat building-code violations, which bears on habitability enforcement and tenant protections.
enrichment.summary: A substitute resolution would establish a Problem Landlord and Housing Court Coordination Task Force to recommend improvements to the City's response to chronic and repeat housing code violations and to coordinate with the Circuit Court of Cook County. It would include City Council members, the Mayor's Office, and several city departments, and report within 180 days.

items.title: Amendment of Municipal Code Section 17-9-0129 allowing lawful cannabis dispensaries to modify to include medical cannabis without triggering Section 17-9-0129.1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance concerns cannabis dispensary operations and zoning standards for cannabis business establishments, with no dwelling units or residential use affected.

items.title: Amendment of Municipal Code Chapter 17-3 by adding Section 17-3-0600 regarding transient-oriented development (TOD) streets

enrichment.relevance_reason: A zoning text amendment creating TOD street rules would require rezonings along designated streets to B or C1 districts with at least 3 FAR and change residential parking and ground-floor design standards near transit.
enrichment.summary: Substitute ordinance from Ald. Matthew J. Martin (47th Ward) would add TOD street rules to the zoning code, designating segments of Ravenswood and Western. Rezonings abutting them would require a B or C1 district with at least 3 FAR, and the existing pedestrian-street exceptions would no longer apply there.

items.title: Designation of segment of N Western Ave right-of-way on Map Nos. 9-H, 9-I, 11-H, 11-I, 13-H, and 13-I as Transient Oriented Development (TOD) Street and amendment of Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F designating portion of N Western Ave as Transient Oriented Development (TOD) Street

attachments.label: TOD Street - Western Avenue - Addison to Ainslie (1)

enrichment.relevance_reason: Designating a stretch of N Western Ave as a TOD street amends the zoning code and typically changes density and parking rules for residential development along it.
enrichment.summary: Aldermen Matthew J. Martin (47th) and Andre Vasquez Jr. (40th) propose designating North Western Avenue from West Addison Street to West Ainslie Street as a Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Street, amending zoning maps and Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F.

items.title: Designation of segment of N Ravenswood Ave right-of-way on Map No. 11-H as Transient Oriented Development (TOD) Street and amendment of Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F designating portion of N Ravenswood Ave as Transient Oriented Development Street

attachments.label: TOD Street -  Ravenswood Avenue - Irving Park to Lawrence

enrichment.relevance_reason: Designating a TOD street in the zoning code changes development standards that can allow more density and reduced parking for housing along the corridor.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Ald. Matthew J. Martin (47th Ward) would designate N. Ravenswood Ave between W. Irving Park Rd and W. Lawrence Ave as a Transit Oriented Development Street, amending the zoning map and Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F.

items.title: Repeal of historical landmark designation for Cortland Bridge

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance repeals a historical landmark designation for the Cortland Bridge, a structure with no dwelling units or residential use, so it does not bear on homes or residents' rights.

items.title: Historical landmark fee waiver for property at 208 S LaSalle St

attachments.label: Permit Fee Waiver - 208 S LaSalle signed

enrichment.relevance_reason: The order waives city permit fees for converting floors of a historic LaSalle Street building into 167 residential units, 30% of them affordable.
enrichment.summary: An order by Alderman Brendan Reilly would waive city permit fees for adaptive reuse of floors 14-16 of the Continental and Commercial National Bank Building into 167 dwelling units, 30% affordable at 60% AMI. The owner is 208 LaSalle Owner, LLC.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map Nos. 1-H and 3-H at 1600-1760 W Chicago Ave and 1601-1759 W Chicago Ave

enrichment.relevance_reason: A city-initiated-style rezoning along West Chicago Avenue moves parcels from B1 neighborhood shopping districts to B3 community shopping districts, which changes the zoning rules that govern residential and mixed-use development there.
enrichment.summary: Ald. Daniel La Spata (1st Ward) proposes rezoning parcels along 1600-1760 W Chicago Ave and 1601-1759 W Chicago Ave from B1-2 and B1-3 to B3-2 and B3-3 community shopping districts. Several parcels with other existing zoning are excluded.

geography.address: 1600-1760 W Chicago Ave and 1601-1759 W Chicago Ave

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 10-F at 4639-4643 S Wallace St

enrichment.relevance_reason: A downzoning from a neighborhood mixed-use district to a single-unit detached house district changes the residential development capacity of the site.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Ald. Raymond A. Lopez (15th Ward) would rezone 4639-43 S Wallace Street from B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District to RS-3 Residential Single Unit (Detached House) District on Map No. 10-F.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 12-F at 5000-5046 S Wells St

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning changes a B1-1 shopping district to RS-3 single-unit residential, altering what homes can be built on the site.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Alderwoman Jeanette B. Taylor (20th Ward) would rezone the area at 5000-5046 S. Wells Street on Map No. 12-F from B1-1 Neighborhood Shopping District to RS-3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached House) District.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 17-H at 1721 W Greenleaf Ave

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would change a site from a residential two-flat, townhouse and multi-unit district to a community shopping district, which could remove residential zoning.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Alderwoman Maria Hadden (49th Ward) would rezone the area at 1721 W. Greenleaf Avenue from RT-4 Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and Multi-Unit District to B3-3 Community Shopping District.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map Nos. 8-F and 10-F at 3800-3958 S State St, 3901-3959 S Dearborn St, 3900-3958 S Dearborn St, 3901-3959 S Federal St, 3900-3946 S Federal St, 2-24 W Pershing Rd, 1-109 W Pershing Rd and 2-52 W 40th St - App No. 23087

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning amends and expands Business Planned Development No. 1143 on largely city-owned land, with a Phase II that includes multi-family housing and an application indicating the ARO applies.
enrichment.summary: P.S. Bronzeville, LLC seeks to rezone RS-3, RT-4 and PD 1143 land near 39th and State to an expanded Business Planned Development No. 1143. Phase I is a grocery-anchored mixed-use development; Phase II, north of Pershing, would include multi-family housing. The city owns part of the site.

geography.address: 3800-3958 S State St, 3901-3959 S Dearborn St, 3900-3958 S Dearborn St, 3901-3959 S Federal St, 3900-3946 S Federal St, 2-24 W Pershing Rd, 1-109 W Pershing Rd and 2-52 W 40th St

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No.  4-E at 1608 S Wabash Ave - App No. 23131

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from DX-5 to DS-3 at 1608 S. Wabash is for a storage and delivery use for construction materials with zero dwelling units, so it neither adds, removes, nor changes homes on the site.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 10-E at 3927-3933 S Martin Luther King, Jr. Dr. - App No. 23135

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from RM-5 to B3-3 is for a vacant lot to be used for a restaurant with zero dwelling units and zero parking, so it is a purely commercial use that adds, removes, and changes no homes even though the old residential district would have allowed them.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 12-K at 5312 S Kenneth Ave - App No. 23172

enrichment.relevance_reason: A residential rezoning of a lot with an existing multi-unit building from RS-2 to RT-4 to bring a three-unit building into zoning compliance.
enrichment.summary: Midway 5312 S. Kenneth Avenue Condominium seeks to rezone 5312 S. Kenneth Avenue from RS-2 to RT-4 to unify the lot under one district. The existing three-unit residential building was built contrary to approved plans; attorney is Mark Kupiec.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 3-I at 1140 N California Ave - App No. 23162T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from B3-1 to B3-3 is for a new 3-story outpatient behavioral health clinic and medical office with no residential units, so it does not bear on homes.
enrichment.summary: Humboldt Park Health seeks a rezoning of 1140 N California Ave from B3-1 to B3-3 Community Shopping District to build a 3-story outpatient behavioral health clinic, urgent care center and medical office with no off-street parking.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 13-L at 4841 N Lipps Ave- App No. 23163

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance reclassifies one site from B3-2 Community Shopping to C1-2 Neighborhood Commercial, both commercial districts, and the text mentions no dwelling units or residential use being added, removed, or changed.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 12-D at 5482 S Ridgewood Ct - App No. 23170T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A residential rezoning from RT-4 to RM-4.5 for a single-family home at 5482 S Ridgewood Ct, which changes the permitted residential density and setbacks.
enrichment.summary: Homeowners Nabil M. Abou Baker and Sara G. Jelinek seek to rezone 5482 S Ridgewood Ct from RT-4 to RM-4.5 to replace a two-story rear addition on their single-family home, with setback and open-space variations. No parking would be provided.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 2-K at 4125 and 4127 W 5th Ave - App No. 23171T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning from RT-4 to RM-4.5 would allow two new three-unit residential buildings on vacant lots near the CTA Pulaski Blue Line station.
enrichment.summary: TECHCO SAVVY INC. seeks to rezone 4125 and 4127 W 5th Ave from RT-4 to RM-4.5 to split the lot and build two three-story buildings, each with three dwelling units, plus setback variations.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 4-H at 2142 W 18th Pl - App No. 23173T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A residential rezoning that would split a lot, legalize an existing five-unit building, and allow a new three-unit building on a vacant lot.
enrichment.summary: Coach House Properties LLC seeks to rezone 2142 W. 18th Place from RT-4 to RM-5 to split the lot, legalizing the existing five-unit building's setbacks and bulk. The vacant lot would stay RT-4 and get a three-unit building.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 7-H at 2315-2317 W Barry Ave - App No. 23169T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning from RS-3 to RT-4 would allow renovation and expansion of an existing three-unit residential building.
enrichment.summary: Rezones 2315-17 W Barry Ave from RS-3 to RT-4 so ZSD Barry LLC can renovate and expand, with a rear addition, an existing three-dwelling-unit residential building. The plans keep three units and four parking spaces.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 5-H at 1933 N Winchester Ave - App No. 23175T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would legalize an existing fifth dwelling unit in a residential building, affecting the permitted housing unit count.
enrichment.summary: Theus Property Holding - 1933 N. Winchester L.L.C. seeks to rezone 1933 N Winchester Ave from RS-3 to RM-4.5 to bring an existing fifth residential unit and dormer into conformance. No expansion of the 2.5-story building is proposed.
entities: Theus Property Holding - 1933 N. Winchester L.L.C.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 15-J at 3244-3250 W Bryn Mawr Ave - App No. 23176T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance as written reclassifies B2-3 to B2-3 with no stated residential units or housing change, so nothing in the material bears on homes.
enrichment.summary: Zoning reclassification on Map No. 15-J for 3244-3250 W Bryn Mawr Ave (App No. 23176T1). The ordinance text lists the area as B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District both before and after the change.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 18-E at 7353-7359 S Indiana Ave - App No. 23148T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A Type 1 rezoning would allow a new 8-unit residential building on a vacant lot, adding homes.
enrichment.summary: The applicant seeks to rezone the vacant lot at 7353-7359 S Indiana Ave from RS2 to RT4 to build a two-story, 8-unit residential building with a 7-car garage. The site is a Transit Served Location.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 1-H at 2156 W Warren Blvd - App No. 23147T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning from RT4 to RM5 to build an 8-unit residential building on a vacant lot adds homes.
enrichment.summary: 2156 W Warren LLC seeks to rezone 2156 W Warren Blvd from RT4 to RM5 to build a new 4-story, 8-unit residential building with 5 parking spaces on a vacant lot. The request also seeks setback and rear yard open space variations.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 2-I at 2400 W Grenshaw St a.k.a. 1124 S Western Ave - App No. 23149T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would allow a new 7-unit residential building, including ground-floor residential use, on a vacant lot.
enrichment.summary: Rezones 2400 W. Grenshaw St. (a.k.a. 1124 S. Western Ave.) from C1-2 to B2-3 to allow a new 4-story, 7-unit residential building with 3 parking spaces. The applicant also seeks a rear setback reduction from 30 feet to 9 feet.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 8-G at 3439 S Morgan St - App No. 23152T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would allow a new six-unit residential building on a vacant lot in Bridgeport.
enrichment.summary: QHN LLC seeks to rezone vacant land at 3439 S Morgan St from B1-3 to B2-3 to build a four-story, six-unit residential building. It also seeks to cut required off-street parking from six spaces to three. The project is not subject to the ARO.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 1-H at 1921 W Chicago Ave - App No. 23153T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would allow a new four-story mixed-use building with three residential units replacing a two-story residence.
enrichment.summary: Rezones 1921 W Chicago Ave from B3-2 to B3-3 Community Shopping District so the applicant can replace a two-story residence with a four-story building holding one ground-floor retail space and three apartments above, with three garage parking spaces.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 3-H at 1807-1809 W Augusta Blvd - App No. 23130T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Type 1 zoning application would allow a new six-unit residential building on a partly vacant lot in the 36th Ward.
enrichment.summary: 1807-09 W. Augusta Blvd LLC seeks a Type 1 map amendment, with administrative adjustments and variations, to build a three-story, six-unit residential building with a five-space detached garage at 1807-09 W. Augusta Blvd. The owner is M15 Land Investments LLC.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 5-H at 1644 N Winchester Ave - App No. 23155T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning from RS-3 to RT-4 would allow a rehabbed single-family home to add an accessory dwelling unit above a new garage.

notices.detail: Department of Housing Proposes Additional Funding for Affordable Senior Housing Development in Humboldt Park

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item seeks additional TIF funding for an affordable senior rental development in Humboldt Park.
enrichment.summary: The Department of Housing is asking City Council to amend a TIF Redevelopment Agreement with an extra $1 million for the 1539 N. Pulaski Elderly Apartments. The money would cover unforeseen structural rehabilitation costs at the historic Pioneer Arcade building. The project has 60 affordable senior units plus one manager's unit.

notices.title: New on Department of Housing home: Department of Housing Seeks Council Approval for Additional Funding for Oak and Larrabee Mixed-Income Development
notices.detail: Department of Housing Seeks Council Approval for Additional Funding for Oak and Larrabee Mixed-Income Development

enrichment.relevance_reason: It seeks added TIF funding for a 78-unit mixed-income rental development on vacant CHA-owned land in Cabrini.
enrichment.summary: The Department of Housing is asking City Council to amend a TIF redevelopment agreement, raising assistance from $14 million to up to $16.7 million for the first phase of Oak and Larrabee. The building would have 78 mixed-income rental units, 54 of them affordable, on CHA-owned land.
